alt: Four checks for each pre-released source: provenance (who, when, for whom, why), content (what it says or shows), context (the events it relates to) and links (other topics it could serve).
caption: Provenance, content, context and links for every pre-released source.

alt: Four rows. Question 1: a supporting detail from the source plus one piece of contextual knowledge. Question 2: state the difference, show it from both sources, explain why they differ. Question 3: what the content shows, confirmed by knowledge, and how provenance makes it useful; limitations are not required. Question 4: plan both sides, link several sources with own knowledge and reach a judgement.
caption: Each question has its own job: support, difference, usefulness, then a judgement.

after: ## Option 1: Peacemaking and the League of Nations, c1919-1939
alt: Three cards give the aims of the Big Three: Clemenceau wanted security and a weaker Germany; Lloyd George wanted to punish Germany but let trade recover; Wilson's Fourteen Points included self-determination and a League. Germany called Versailles a Diktat. The wider settlement: Saint-Germain and Neuilly (1919), Trianon and Sèvres (1920), with Sèvres replaced by Lausanne (1923).
caption: Different aims among the Big Three, and five treaties beyond Versailles.

after: ## Option 1: Peacemaking and the League of Nations, c1919-1939
alt: A timeline of the League: Vilna (1920) a failure; the Aaland Islands and Upper Silesia (1921) settled; Corfu (1923) bypassed by the Conference of Ambassadors; Bulgaria (1925) settled; Locarno and Kellogg-Briand outside the League; Germany joins (1926); Japan invades Manchuria (1931); Germany and Japan leave (1933); the USSR joins (1934); Italy invades Abyssinia (1935); Italy leaves (1937).
caption: Some successes in the 1920s; great powers bypassed or defied the League, above all in the 1930s.

after: ## Option 2: Crises of the Cold War, 1960-1975
alt: A timeline: Castro takes power in 1959; the Bay of Pigs invasion fails in April 1961; in October 1962 U2 photographs reveal Soviet missile sites and Kennedy announces a quarantine; after thirteen days Khrushchev removes the missiles in return for a no-invasion pledge and the secret removal of US missiles from Turkey; a hotline and the Partial Test Ban Treaty follow in 1963.
caption: Thirteen days of crisis ended in a trade, then new steps to manage the risk.

after: ## Option 2: Crises of the Cold War, 1960-1975
alt: A timeline of US involvement in Vietnam: Kennedy increases advisers and backs Strategic Hamlets; the Gulf of Tonkin incident (1964); bombing and ground troops from 1965; the Tet Offensive and My Lai (1968); Nixon's Vietnamisation; Kent State (1970); Nixon in China (1972); the Paris Peace Accords (1973); and the fall of Saigon in April 1975.
caption: Escalation to 1968, then a turn against the war and a staged withdrawal.
